newsitem.title: USA: San Diego County, Calif., ratings cut to new low.
newsitem.headline: San Diego County, Calif., ratings cut to new low.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service Inc. on Thursday cut some of San Diego County's debt ratings to a new low, warning that the southern California county's fiscal flexibility and credit position had weakened.
Bill Kelly, San Diego County's assistant auditor-controller, said the Moody's move would increase the county's borrowing costs in the future.

"We're disappointed in the action taken by Moody's but understand the pressure they're under in rating counties whose flexibility has been limited by actions of the state," Kelly said after the Moody's announcement.

Moody's said fiscal pressures -- from state revenue reductions and the lingering effects of the recession, to problems related to its solid waste system and investment pool -- had strained the county's fiscal position.
Moody's said the downgrade also reflected factors common to all California counties, including the added burden associated with new federal welfare reform.
Moody's said it would monitor the situation going forward.
"I don't think any further action is imminent," said Moody's Vice President Nikolai Sklaroff. But he added, "This is a situation that hasn't reached its final resolution."

Moody's lowered San Diego County long-term obligations to Baa1 from single-A. Baa1, considered a medium grade rating, is a single notch below single-A, an upper-medium grade rating. Baa1 is several steps below the highest rating of AAA.
The Baa1 rating was a new low for these obligations.
